messages:
lina: Heads-up — seeing ECC corrected errors spike on rack27 (nodes rack27-0..rack27-3). 4 GPUs with rising ECC corrected counts and intermittent Xid 13 / Xid 136 kernel messages in dmesg. Spike started ~01:30 UTC. Suspect thermal or power flicker, not a software regression. Anyone oncall/near that colo?

infra-bot: [ALERT] ecc.errors.corrected.rate > threshold on rack27 (id: alert-ec-827). 4 affected GPUs. samples: 180, 240, 195, 210 errors/min.

raj: Can we cordon + drain the nodes now? I'll start live-migrating inference pods off rack27 and fail open to fallback pool.

lina: yes please — cordon first, then drain. I'll create a maintenance ticket and start the RMA prep.

raj: kubectl commands I ran for the first node (example):
```
kubectl cordon rack27-0
kubectl drain rack27-0 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app!=critical-fallback' --timeout=10m
```
Do that for rack27-0..3 sequentially to avoid capacity loss.

tessa: FYI — last time we saw a similar pattern (rack19) it ended up being a flaky riser + a PDU phase imbalance. Symptoms were: ECC spikes coincident with transient voltage dips and fan RPM drop. We swapped riser and updated BMC firmware, counts dropped. Recommend checking ipmi sensor data and PDU logs before swapping GPUs.

sam: I'm on-site and can be there in ~25m to check PDUs and reseat cards if needed. I can also take thermal pics.

lina: thanks Sam. I'll post the serials and a minimal RMA description so we can escalate quickly:
```
Affected GPUs (rack27):
- GPU-A SN: RW-9A1K-00123
- GPU-B SN: RW-9A1K-00124
- GPU-C SN: RW-9A1K-00125
- GPU-D SN: RW-9A1K-00126
Symptoms: ECC corrected error surge, intermittent Xid 13/136, no driver changes in last 72h. Suspected hardware/power/thermal.
```
I'll open vendor ticket and reference prior batch id 2024-Q4 lot if they ask.

raj: Immediate mitigations that helped before:
- add taint: node.kubernetes.io/under-maintenance:NoSchedule
- move traffic to dedicated fallback pool (use routing weight shift)
- enable per-GPU traffic caps in gateway for that rack
Also add a short-term alert rule: if ecc.corrected.rate > 150 for >2m, auto-taint node and notify oncall.

tessa: Commands to pull quick diagnostics before doing hardware work:
```
# ECC counters by type
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=uuid,name,fan.speed,temperature.gpu,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile.32bit,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile.32bit --format=csv -i 0,1,2,3
# detailed logs
journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -o short-iso | tail -n 200
# BMC sensors
ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U admin -P <pw> sensor
```
Collect those and attach to the RMA.

sam: On-site update: PDUs show slight phase imbalance on PDU-B (L2 current 3.1A higher than L1/L3). Rack fans look dusty but spinning. I reseated power connectors on rack27-1 and rack27-2, re-plugged two riser power cables. Doing a controlled reboot of rack27-1 now via BMC.

infra-bot: [INFO] maintenance ticket created: #INC-2026-8492. RMA prep doc assigned to lina.

lina: After Sam reseat and reboot we saw ECC counts on rack27-1 drop from ~210/min -> 12/min within 6 minutes. rack27-2 still elevated. Good sign power/riser is likely culprit.

raj: Ok lets not replace GPUs yet. Plan: 1) replace risers and power leads for affected nodes, 2) run 24h validation with gpu-burn / targeted workloads, 3) if counts remain >50/min escalate RMA for GPU swap.

tessa: Also add long-term telemetry: correlate ecc.error spikes with PDU phase, BMC reported fan RPM, inlet temp, and node power draw. I can add a Grafana panel and a synthetic probe.

lina: Action items:
- sam: swap risers + power leads for rack27-2 and 27-3, validate, ETA 4h (owner: sam)
- raj: add temporary auto-taint alert and traffic shift runbook, ETA 1h (owner: raj)
- tessa: dashboard + correlation job for PDU/BMC/ecc, ETA 2d (owner: tessa)
- lina: open vendor RMA & attach diagnostics (ticket created), ETA 30m to vendor outreach

sam: Will also collect BMC serials and FW versions and check for matching lot firmware bug in vendor KB.

lina: notes for postmortem (we'll convert to formal RCA if pattern repeats):
- probable root cause: intermittent power/riser issues causing transient voltage dips -> GPU memory ECC corrections + kernel Xid events.
- contributing: dusty fans/thermal, no PDU phase imbalance alert previously, no per-rack power observability in alerting.
- mitigations: riser/power swap, firmware updates, auto-taint rule, better telemetry on PDU phase/power.

raj: I'll start drafting a short postmortem and include timeline + graphs once tessa has panels.

tessa: I'll add the comparator panel for rack19 historical incident too — to see if there's same signature.

lina: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread for timeline + final RCA. If counts re-spike after riser swap we'll do GPU replacements.

sam: On-site finish update: swapped riser + power leads on rack27-2 and rack27-3. Both nodes stable after 90m validation (gpu-burn 30m + workload replay). Moving nodes back into service now.

infra-bot: [RESOLVED] alert-ec-827 lower than threshold for 45m.

lina: marking incident as resolved for now. I'll put a follow-up RCA doc in /confluence and link back.

raj: +1. Recommend we add preventive riser inspection to quarterly ops checklist for racks with high utilization.

(End of thread)
